incident-bot: [INCIDENT created] IR-2026-142 · node-ml-gpu-07: CUDA OOM reported by inference runtime, customer-facing errors starting ~08:02 UTC :rotating_light:

maria: seeing a bunch of 500s for model 'redwood-7b' from pod runtime-ml-07. stack shows CUDA OOM even though nvidia-smi reports ~4.8GB free on GPU0.

ryan_oncall: on it. can someone paste the pod logs and nvidia-smi output?

maria: pasted below:
```
$ kubectl logs runtime-ml-07 -c inference --tail=200
E tensorflow: cuda runtime error (2): out of memory at src/runtime.c:123
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve.py", line 210, in handle_request
    tokens = model.generate(req)
  File "/opt/runtime/engine.py", line 890, in generate
    self.kv_cache.reserve(seq_len)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```

and
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB]
24432 MiB, 18912 MiB
```

sre_jen: so ~5.5GiB free but OOM still thrown. suspect fragmentation or reserved blocks held by another process or driver accounting mismatch. any long-lived processes?

kevin_infra: checked node: docker ps shows a sidecar collector (kv-keeper) pinned to GPU0 but it's at low usage. trying `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` now.

maria: customer impact: CS reporting 12% of requests for tenant AcmeCorp are failing with 500s since 08:02 UTC. escalation opened.

incident-bot: [pager duty] paging ryan_oncall (level: P1)

ryan_oncall: taking. quick hypothesis: allocator reserved pool vs runtime headroom mismatch after a recent allocator tweak (PR #4123) that changed reserve semantics. could be that the reserve accounting shows available global free but per-allocator reserved slabs are fragmented.

sre_jen: while ryans on it, I'm going to check dmesg and driver logs for CUDA errors and any OOM kill.

kevin_infra: output: 
```
GPU 0: FB Memory Usage
  Total                       : 24432 MiB
  Used                        : 18912 MiB
  Free                        :  5519 MiB
  Reserved by driver           : 2048 MiB
  Allocated (blocks)          : 16384 MiB

Driver info shows repeated warnings: "Reserved memory block too fragmented to fulfill request"
```

maria: that driver message looks new. did we roll any kernel/driver update?

kevin_infra: we rolled cudart 12.2.1 -> 12.3.0 on 03/10 in the infra cohort for perf patches. it increased default reservation granularity.

ryan_oncall: OK that matches. mitigation plan: 1) mark node-ml-gpu-07 Unschedulable, 2) drain inference pods off node to stop alloc churn, 3) restart GPU daemon and runtime to clear fragmented reserved blocks, 4) optionally evict long-running sidecars to free reserved slabs.

maria: can we avoid a full restart? customers hit. maybe a rolling restart of the runtime container first (faster) to force allocator to reinit and free soft reserves.

ryan_oncall: try that first. maria, do `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-ml-gpu-07` (or just restart pods on that node). I will coordinate drain if restart doesn't help.

maria: doing quick restart of inference pod now.

maria: restart done. monitoring logs...

maria: post-restart logs: generation requests start succeeding again but intermittent OOMs persist during long sequences. 500 rate down from 12% -> 3%.

ryan_oncall: good partial relief. still not safe. let's drain node and move workloads for a clean slate. scheduling a drain with `kubectl drain node-ml-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

kevin_infra: warning: draining will evict kv-keeper and some monitoring agents; will spin up replacement nodes. scheduling now.

incident-bot: [action] node-ml-gpu-07 cordoned at 08:26 UTC by ryan_oncall

sre_jen: during drain I noticed the runtime heap shows many small pinned allocations in CUDA driver reported with sizes ~32KiB and ~64KiB which aligns with fragmentation pattern. suspect per-request small allocations are never coalesced due to new reserve granularity.

maria: quick mitigation idea: enable smaller slab coalescing at runtime config: `ALLOCATOR_COALESCE=true` and reduce reserve slab size to 8MB from 64MB. can we patch deployment and roll?

kevin_infra: that config change is low-risk and can be rolled via config map. I'll apply to staging then prod if staging confirms. applying to staging now.

maria: staging test passed under synthetic load. applying to prod with canary 10% across nodes.

maria: canary rolled to a subset of nodes. metrics show lower OOMs and lower 500 rate for the canary.

ryan_oncall: after canary stability, roll to remaining nodes. also recording root cause: driver reserve semantics + recent cudart bump changed allocation granularity -> increased fragmentation -> existing reserve accounting showed free memory but blocks couldn't satisfy contiguous allocation -> runtime threw OOM.

cs-alex: FYI I'm updating AcmeCorp ticket: temporary mitigation applied (restart + config patch), expected full rollback in 40m. notifying them and offering dedicated reroute if they see residual errors.

incident-bot: [update] IR-2026-142: partial mitigation applied, customer impact reduced to <1%. postmortem scheduled.

ryan_oncall: next steps: 1) finish roll of ALLOCATOR_COALESCE config, 2) coordinate with infra to evaluate driver downgrade vs long-term allocator improvements, 3) add a runtime health probe to detect fragmentation pattern earlier, 4) create a postmortem and link PRs (allocator revert PR #4123 and coalesce PR #4188).

sre_jen: grabbing logs and heap dumps for postmortem, and adding an observable to track contiguous-block failures from driver.

maria: thanks all. handing off to kevin for infra follow-up and to jen for postmortem. ryan, will you ack closure when rollout completes?

ryan_oncall: will confirm when all nodes show stable error rates for 30m. leaving this thread open for status updates. :white_check_mark:
